terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A welded galvanised barrier panel: one rigid frame on two fixed feet. Nothing opens, turns or swings on the prop itself -- the feet swivel in life but ship fixed across the run -- and the hook and eye are silhouette, not sockets, since linking is done by placing the next panel. One root pivot and zero sockets. Event fronts, temple fairs, motorcade routes, road closures; links into runs. Spangled zinc scratched all over, rust bled from every weld and down the ends, flat bar feet scuffed pale.

reasoning: ONE tube frame -- the uprights and top rail with 0.12 m rounded corners as a single SWEPT polyline, the bottom rail, five bar tubes, two foot stubs, an eye ring and two hook brackets, and twelve conical weld beads -- merged on one material; ONE component of five pressed infill panels, each a returned rim over a recessed face; and ONE component of two flat feet. THREE draw calls of four.

The feet are their own component because the UV mode, not the material, forces it: height UVs write v = y / scale, so every vertex of a foot top face lands on the same row of the tile and the whole face samples one texel line. The feet shipped flat and khaki because of it. Triplanar world UVs on that component alone fix it, at one draw call and no second material.
One material: galvanised steel as vertex colours on white -- zinc, a paler sheet, grey foot bar, rust-brown weld beads -- with one 1024 px hot-dip zinc canvas after construction.
No repetition system: five panels differ in width (the open bay breaks the rhythm), so they are five rim-and-face pairs in one merge rather than an InstancedMesh.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the rounded-corner tube frame with stub-mounted flat feet and the bay pattern the plate shows -- five sheeted bays and one open one near the +X end; the tubes are real swept cylinders because their round highlight is what reads galvanised at distance, and the panels are pressed pans rather than flat plates because the returned rim's shadow line is what says sheet metal rather than card.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The bay pattern follows the plate (five sheets, one open bay) rather than the proxy (two open bays).

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 2.00 x 1.10 x 0.45 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 1.84 m wide, 1.10 m tall closed tube rectangle with 0.12 m rounded top corners, standing on two stubs at +-0.67 that drop to 0.55 m flat feet; a bottom rail at 0.30 m closing the frame; five vertical bar tubes dividing it into six bays, five of them sheeted; an eye at 0.55 m on -X, hook brackets at 0.53 and 0.885 m on +X.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -1.043..+0.987: the uprights at +-0.92 with the eye reaching -1.043 and the hooks +0.987; y 0.00 to 1.10 at the top rail crown; z +-0.275 at the 0.55 m feet (declared 0.45: the feet overrun the declared depth by 0.05 m each side, and the collider is set to the declared). The frame is a CLOSED tube rectangle: the uprights and the five bars die into the bottom rail at 0.30 m and stop there, and the panel stands on two stubs at +-0.67 that drop into the centre of each foot. That is read off the +X end of the plate, where the crown, the ground and the rail are all legible at one x (ground y=745 px, crown y=86, so 0.001669 m/px; rail underside 578 and foot top 718 give a 0.234 m stub, i.e. a rail centre at 0.045 + 0.234 + 0.021 = 0.30). The -X end of the same plate draws the upright running past the rail to the foot instead; a generated plate is not projectively consistent, and the +X reading is the one that agrees with the class. Stub x from the plate fraction 0.15 at the near end and 0.88 at the far, which bound the model fraction from either side of the perspective. The proxy normalises to w:h 1:0.635 including the hooks, i.e. 1.33 H for the panel itself; the DECLARED 2.00 x 1.10 (1.82 H) is the registry contract for a standard panel and is what is built, so the band table's +0.33 H width residual is the declared aspect, not the build.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.901 x 1.208 x 0.554 hooks included. Occupancy map (scratch/_mon/occupancy.mjs): top rail 0.92-0.98 H, bottom rail 0.34-0.40 H, two open bays -- the plate shows ONE, at the fifth position, and the plate is the authority for the pattern. The rail is built at 0.30 m (0.27 H) on the plate measurement above rather than the proxy band, which is a reconstruction of the same ambiguity the plate has at its near end. Band table: mean |delta depth| 0.0175 H; width +0.33 H by the declared aspect (arithmetic above).

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: a barrier panel is the same from both faces; the sheets are centred in the frame plane.

componentTree.name: Tube frame, rail, feet and hooks
componentTree.topologyRationale: One SWEPT polyline for the uprights and rounded-corner top rail, the bottom rail, five bars, two foot stubs, two hook brackets and the eye stem, plus the eye ring lathe and twelve conical weld beads: one merge, one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Tubes r 0.021 (frame), 0.019 (bars), 0.0231 (bottom rail) and 0.0164 (stubs); uprights at x +-0.92 from the rail at 0.30 up to 1.079 m; corners r 0.12; stubs at +-0.67 from 0.018 to the rail.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: No two tubes that meet share a radius. The bottom rail is FATTER than the uprights that die into it and the stubs are THINNER than the rail they hang from, so every end cap is swallowed with millimetres to spare -- equal radii are tangent, and tangent surfaces z-fight into a white sliver that reads as a hole at the weld. Bar ends stop inside both rails as interpenetrating solids; the beads straddle the rail surface. Nothing planar meets.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 1.15 m, which is what puts the tile's rust bands at the feet and along the crown.

localFeatures.delivery: swept tubes and a ring lathe

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Zinc as vertex colour on white steel with a hot-dip spangle canvas; weld beads #826e58.

pivot.name: root

componentTree.name: Pressed sheet infill panels
componentTree.topologyRationale: Five pressed pans of differing widths in one merge on the frame's material: one draw call, and separable for part coverage.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Each pan fills its bay from the bottom rail to the top rail, 8 mm clear of every tube: a 13 mm returned rim extruded from z -0.007 to +0.006, and a face 4 mm thick recessed to z -0.005..-0.001.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The face OVERLAPS the rim opening by 7 mm rather than meeting its reveal, and no bounding plane of the two coincides in any axis. The pans are 8 mm clear of every tube. check-coplanar reports clean at 1 mm.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 1.15 m.

localFeatures.delivery: five extruded rims over five recessed faces

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Zinc sheet as vertex colour on the same white steel, carrying the same spangle canvas.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Flat bar feet
componentTree.topologyRationale: Two flat bars in their own merge -- not for the material, which they share, but for the UV MODE: height UVs give a horizontal face one texel row, and the feet shipped flat and khaki because of it. World (triplanar) UVs on this component alone, at one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: 0.075 x 0.045 x 0.55 m bars centred under the stubs at x +-0.67, on the ground.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The stubs enter the feet from above as interpenetrating solids and the beads straddle the top face; nothing planar meets.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 0.55 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Foot bar tone as vertex colour on the same white steel.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/zinc.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: weld beads at every bar and stub end, and the ground and crown bands
localOverrides.evidence: Measured over the whole plate: pixels with R-B > 26 are 2.2%% of the frame at mean #826e58. Carried as twelve conical weld beads at that tone plus the tile's own rust bands, which height UVs at 1.15 m put at the feet and along the top rail -- the two places the plate has it. The first build carried it as ten flat #8a6a4a boxes 42 x 20 mm, which rendered as orange stickers.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-zinc (0.86) at #8f9394 sd 35 (cloudy zinc) and region-rail at #939391; matched flat panel crops of the plate read mean luma 157-159 at sd 12-16 with p5..p95 of 139..181.

Albedo is authored for the HARNESS TRANSFER, not copied from the plate. The panel face measures R = 0.89 A (albedo 164 rendered 146 with the tile at 1.0), and the canvas is a MULTIPLY map whose mean multiplier measures 0.72, so a target luma T wants an albedo of T / 0.64. Every tone below is the plate measurement times that factor, written as hex x factor so a re-measure is one number: zinc #9a9d9e x1.48, sheet #9ba0a0 x1.55, feet #787a78 x1.62, weld beads #826e58 x1.10. Rendered back: panel mean 152-164, sd 9-13, p5..p95 131..179 against the plate's 157-159 / 12-16 / 139..181.
Metalness 0.30, not physical: the thaikit harness has no environment map and a full metal renders black.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 1024 px hot-dip zinc canvas after construction -- drift, clustered spangle, fine grain, scratches, drip streaks and rust bled from the ground and crown bands -- built in 117 ms for 5.3 MB of texture VRAM. 1024 rather than 512 because the tile spans 1.15 m and the plate resolves the panels at ~4.5 px/cm; 512 gives 2.2 and reads as smooth grey with snow on it however the histogram is tuned.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components, no repetition system: 3 of 4. The third is the feet, forced by the UV mode rather than the material.

materials.note: steel only: 1 of 3; sheet, feet and weld beads are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,980 of 4,000: one 18-point swept frame outline at 12 segments, ten short swept tubes, twelve 8-segment bead cones, one ring lathe, five extruded rims and seven boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: SWEPT polyline tubes for every rail, bar, stub and hook -- one mitred ring per point rather than a cylinder per segment, because the per-segment builder extends each cylinder by 1.2 r to close its joints and a 0.12 m corner has a 0.038 m chord, so the bend rendered as an accordion of pleats. A small ring lathe for the eye; tapered cones for the weld beads; extruded rectangular rings and boxes for the pans; boxes for the feet.
No InstancedMesh: the five sheets differ in width. In a scene the HOST instances the whole panel along a run.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 1024 px hot-dip zinc canvas after construction, 5.3 MB of texture VRAM, built in 117 ms.

risks.description: The plate draws the -X leg running past the bottom rail to the foot and the +X leg stopping at the rail. Only one can be true.
risks.mitigation: Built to the +X reading, which is the standard barrier and the end where the crown, ground and rail are all legible at one x. Recorded as an assumption with the arithmetic; a second plate would settle it.

risks.description: The proxy reads the panel at 1.33 H wide; the declared 2.00 x 1.10 is 1.82 H.
risks.mitigation: The registry notes fix 2.00 m as the standard panel; the plate is a foreshortened three-quarter view. Built to the declaration; residual recorded with the arithmetic.

risks.description: The open bay and the gaps around every sheet are background enclosed by the silhouette.
risks.mitigation: The turntable gate is run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement -- the prop is an open frame by nature.

risks.description: At 90/270 the panel is 0.55 m of feet under a 0.045 m frame, 0.275 of the front width.
risks.mitigation: Collapse ratio passed from the declared depth over the built width.
